header: DO NOT EDIT: regenerate with `python3 proofs/verus/gen_pin_tests.py <spec> --run`.
Each test mirrors one [pins] row of proofs/verus/grep_literal_fold_sync.txt and
drives the REAL analysis (`grep_output`, `word_boundary_hit`), not a copy of it.
`grep_none` rows are the fold's REFUSALS: the parse must answer None so the
shell-out stays. Where a row records a divergence from bash, the note says so.

pins.note: a literal pattern selects the line that contains it -- bash prints the same line
a match at offset 0 is found: the scan starts there
`-w` inside a word: the following byte is a word byte, so there is no whole-word occurrence
`-w` after a space: non-word byte on the left, line edge on the right
`-i` lowers BOTH the pattern and the line before the same test
`-B 1` prints one line of leading context, clamped at the start of the file
a pattern carrying a metacharacter is refused: the matcher is literal-only
a second plain word is a file operand: different streams, so refused
`-A` needs a numeric argument; a non-number refuses the fold
no match: the body is empty. DIVERGENCE d1: the fold also emits status_exec(true), while bash exits 1
DIVERGENCE d3: the empty pattern matches every element of split('\n'), including the phantom trailing one, so the body carries one newline more than bash prints
